Peak of hormesis and substrate inhibition curves

Source: R/ed.R
peak.Rd

The dose at which a curve of the hormesis models braincousens and cedergreen, or of the substrate inhibition model haldane, reaches its maximum, and the maximal response, as MAX in drc. For the hormesis models the peak has no closed form: it is found numerically, and its derivatives, for the standard errors, follow from the implicit function theorem, as for the effective doses of ed. Curves without a stimulation (b5 <= 0) have no peak, and give NA with a warning; the hormesis models need a decreasing curve (b3 < 0), otherwise an error is raised. For haldane, the peak is at the dose sqrt(b4/b5), the optimal substrate concentration sqrt(Km Ki); without inhibition (b5 = 0) there is no peak. With a curvelink, the peak dose is that of the curve, as the link is monotone, and the response at the peak is on the scale of the response, the inverse link of the curve at the peak.

Usage

peak(x, linfct = NULL, newdata = NULL, random = TRUE, vcov. = NULL)

Arguments

x

a drmTMB object of the braincousens, cedergreen or haldane model

linfct, newdata, random

the curves, as in ed

vcov.

the covariance of the estimated parameters, as in ed

Value

an edTMB object, with entries "dose:curve" and "response:curve"; not available for fits in the BMD parameterisation

Details

The result is an edTMB object, as from ed, with the dose and the response at the peak of each curve, named "dose" and "response", and their joint covariance matrix, e.g. for glht of multcomp. confint.edTMB gives Wald and bootstrap intervals for both, and profile likelihood intervals for the dose; for the response, profile intervals are not available and Wald intervals are returned, with a message.

See also

ed, confint.edTMB, edTMB-methods

Examples

# hormesis: stimulation of the growth of lettuce at low concentrations of isobutyl alcohol
hmod <- drmTMB(weight ~ conc, data = lettuce, model = "braincousens")
(p <- peak(hmod))
#> Peak of the hormesis curves, dose and response:
#> 
#>              Estimate Std.Error
#> dose:lf1         0.72    0.2670
#> response:lf1     1.20    0.0694
confint(p, method = "wald")
#>                  2.5 %   97.5 %
#> dose:lf1     0.1162045 1.324228
#> response:lf1 1.0438171 1.357752
# the dose at which the response returns to the level of the control
ed(hmod, respLev = 0)
#> Effective dose estimates:
#> 
#>       Estimate Std.Error
#> 0:lf1     2.93      1.05
